					<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">
</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">Canadian historian and author (1931–2019)</div>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1316064257">.mw-parser-output .infobox-subbox{padding:0;border:none;margin:-3px;width:auto;min-width:100%;font-size:100%;clear:none;float:none;background-color:transparent;color:inherit}.mw-parser-output .infobox-3cols-child{margin:-3px}.mw-parser-output .infobox .navbar{font-size:100%}@media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .infobox-full-data:not(.notheme)>div:not(.notheme)[style]{background:#1f1f23!important;color:#f8f9fa}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .infobox-full-data:not(.notheme)>div:not(.notheme)[style]{background:#1f1f23!important;color:#f8f9fa}}@media(min-width:640px){body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table{display:table!important}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table>caption{display:table-caption!important}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table>tbody{display:table-row-group}body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table th,body.skin--responsive .mw-parser-output .infobox-table td{padding-left:inherit;padding-right:inherit}}</style><table class="infobox biography vcard"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above"><div class="fn">Bruce W. Hodgins</div></th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-image"><span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Frameless"><a href="/wiki/File:Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/45/Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg/250px-Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/45/Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg/387px-Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/45/Bruce_Hodgins_photo.jpeg 2x" data-file-width="387" data-file-height="258" /></a></span></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Born</th><td class="infobox-data"><span style="display:none">(<span class="bday">1931-01-29</span>)</span>January 29, 1931<br /><div style="display:inline" class="birthplace"><a href="/wiki/Kitchener,_Ontario" title="Kitchener, Ontario">Kitchener, Ontario</a></div><span style="display:none" data-plural="1"></span></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Died</th><td class="infobox-data">August 8, 2019<span style="display:none">(2019-08-08)</span> (aged&#160;88)<br /><div style="display:inline" class="deathplace"><a href="/wiki/Peterborough,_Ontario" title="Peterborough, Ontario">Peterborough, Ontario</a></div><span style="display:none" data-plural="1"></span></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Alma&#160;mater</th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Waterloo_College" class="mw-redirect" title="Waterloo College">Waterloo College</a>, <a href="/wiki/Queen%27s_University_at_Kingston" title="Queen&#39;s University at Kingston">Queen's University at Kingston</a>, <a href="/wiki/Duke_University" title="Duke University">Duke University</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Occupations</th><td class="infobox-data role">Historian, author</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Employer</th><td class="infobox-data org"><a href="/wiki/Trent_University" title="Trent University">Trent University</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Organization</th><td class="infobox-data org"><a href="/wiki/Canadian_Canoe_Museum" title="Canadian Canoe Museum">Canadian Canoe Museum</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Political party</th><td class="infobox-data org"><a href="/wiki/New_Democratic_Party" title="New Democratic Party">New Democratic Party</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Awards</th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Canadian_Historical_Association" title="Canadian Historical Association">Canadian Historical Association's</a> <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Historical_Association#Prizes" title="Canadian Historical Association">Clio Award for the North</a> (2000)</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><b>Bruce W. Hodgins</b> (January 29, 1931 – August 8, 2019) was a Canadian academic historian and author.
</p><p>He was a co-founder of <a href="/wiki/Trent_University" title="Trent University">Trent University's</a> history department, a federal <a href="/wiki/New_Democratic_Party" title="New Democratic Party">New Democratic Party</a> candidate, and a co-founder of the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Canoe_Museum" title="Canadian Canoe Museum">Canadian Canoe Museum</a>.
</p><p>He was the author of the 2003 book <i>Blockades and resistance</i> and the co-author of the 1989 book <i>Temagami Experience.</i>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Early_life_and_education">Early life and education</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Bruce_Hodgins&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Early life and education"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Bruce Hodgins was born on January 29, 1931, in <a href="/wiki/Kitchener,_Ontario" title="Kitchener, Ontario">Kitchener, Ontario</a>. His father, Stanley Hodgins, was a school principal and his mother Laura Belle Hodgins (<a href="/wiki/Birth_name" title="Birth name">née</a> Turel) was a nurse. He had a younger brother named Larry.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins studied at <a href="/wiki/Wilfrid_Laurier_University" title="Wilfrid Laurier University">Waterloo College</a> and <a href="/wiki/Queen%27s_University_at_Kingston" title="Queen&#39;s University at Kingston">Queen's University at Kingston</a><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and had a PhD from <a href="/wiki/Duke_University" title="Duke University">Duke University</a> in <a href="/wiki/North_Carolina" title="North Carolina">North Carolina</a> where he attended from 1958.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Career">Career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Bruce_Hodgins&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Canadian_Canoe_Museum.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Canadian_Canoe_Museum.JPG/250px-Canadian_Canoe_Museum.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Canadian_Canoe_Museum.JPG/500px-Canadian_Canoe_Museum.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption>Inside the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Canoe_Museum" title="Canadian Canoe Museum">Canadian Canoe Museum</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Hodgins taught Canadian history and worked in the history departments of <a href="/wiki/Prince_of_Wales_College" title="Prince of Wales College">Prince of Wales College</a> and at the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Western_Ontario" title="University of Western Ontario">University of Western Ontario</a> as well as with Trent University's <a href="/wiki/Leslie_Frost" title="Leslie Frost">Leslie M. Frost Centre for Canadian Heritage and Development Studies</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He was a specialist in the study of <a href="/wiki/John_Sandfield_Macdonald" title="John Sandfield Macdonald">John Sandfield Macdonald</a>, <a href="/wiki/Temagami" title="Temagami">Temagami</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Charles_Alfred_Marie_Paradis&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Charles Alfred Marie Paradis (page does not exist)">Charles Alfred Marie Paradis</a> <a href="https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles-Alfred-Marie_Paradis" class="extiw" title="fr:Charles-Alfred-Marie Paradis"><small>[FR]</small></a>, the <a href="/wiki/Colonization_of_Canada" class="mw-redirect" title="Colonization of Canada">colonization of Canada</a>, Camp Wanapitei, <a href="/wiki/Canadian_federalism" class="mw-redirect" title="Canadian federalism">Canadian federalism</a>, and his home town of <a href="/wiki/Peterborough,_Ontario" title="Peterborough, Ontario">Peterborough, Ontario</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Along with Alan Wilson, he was a co-founder of <a href="/wiki/Trent_University" title="Trent University">Trent University's</a> history department,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> where he worked as a professor from 1965, being promoted to associate professor in 1967.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He retired in 1996.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:3&#95;4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins was the chair of the National Administrative Committee for the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Association_in_Canada" title="United Nations Association in Canada">United Nations Association Canada</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;2-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> With John Jennings, Hodgins was a co-founder of the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Canoe_Museum" title="Canadian Canoe Museum">Canadian Canoe Museum</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins was the <a href="/wiki/New_Democratic_Party" title="New Democratic Party">New Democratic Party</a> candidate for <a href="/wiki/Peterborough%E2%80%94Kawartha" class="mw-redirect" title="Peterborough—Kawartha">Peterborough—Kawartha</a> in the <a href="/wiki/1968_Canadian_federal_election" title="1968 Canadian federal election">1968 Canadian federal election</a>, losing to <a href="/wiki/Hugh_Faulkner_(politician)" title="Hugh Faulkner (politician)">Hugh Faulkner</a>, and remaining an active party member throughout his adult life.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins won the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Historical_Association" title="Canadian Historical Association">Canadian Historical Association's</a> <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Historical_Association#Prizes" title="Canadian Historical Association">Clio Award for the North</a> in 2000.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Selected_publications">Selected publications</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Bruce_Hodgins&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Selected publications"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li>Bruce Hodgins and Jamie Benidickson, <i>Temagami Experience</i> (1989) <a href="/wiki/University_of_Toronto_Press" title="University of Toronto Press">University of Toronto Press</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:4&#95;6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Bruce Hodgins, <i>Blockades and resistance: Studies in actions of peace and the Temagami blockades of 1988-89</i> (2003) <a href="/wiki/Wilfrid_Laurier_University_Press" title="Wilfrid Laurier University Press">Wilfrid Laurier University Press</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:4&#95;6-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>
<li><i>The Canoe in Canadian Cultures/Bark, Skin and Cedar</i> (1999) Natural Heritage/Natural History (co-editor with John Jennings and Doreen Small).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Bruce Hodgins, <i>Nastawgan: The Canadian North by Canoe and Snowshoe</i> (1995) Betelgeuse Books</li>
<li><i>Changing Parks: The History, Future and Cultural Context of Parks and Heritage Landscapes (1998)</i> (co-editor) Toronto: Natural Heritage/Natural History Inc.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Personal_life">Personal life</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Bruce_Hodgins&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Personal life"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Hodgins met Carol, his wife-to-be, in <a href="/wiki/Charlottetown" title="Charlottetown">Charlottetown</a>, while working at the Prince of Wales College.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> They had sons Shawn and Geoff and daughter Gillian Nesbitt.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He moved to Peterborough, Ontario in 1965<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:3&#95;4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and lived on Engleburn Place.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins was a supporter of the Peterborough Historical Society.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> With other family members, he was a part owner of Camp Wanapitei, purchased in 1956.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;3-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Hodgins was one of over 300 people arrested in 1989 for taking part in a protest of a road expansion in Temagami.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> 
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1320445320">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Temagami_Land_Caution" title="Temagami Land Caution">Temagami Land Caution</a></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Death">Death</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Bruce_Hodgins&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Death"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Hodgins died on August 8, 2019, at <a href="/wiki/Peterborough_Regional_Health_Centre" title="Peterborough Regional Health Centre">Peterborough Regional Health Centre</a>, aged 88, after what was presumed to be a series of small strokes.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:2&#95;1-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>
</p>
